unit.why: A single complete narrative: R. Michel of Zlotchov sends a man to a rich man in Berdichev to learn trust in God, and the man is then rewarded on his way home.
unit.boundary_note: Opens with 'ומעשה כזו היתה ג״כ', so it is introduced as a parallel to a preceding tale, but it is self-contained.

stories.start_quote: ומעשה כזו היתה ג״כ בדור שלפנינו
stories.summary_en: R. Michel of Zlotchov rebukes a man for lacking trust in God and sends him to learn it from a rich man in Berdichev. The rich man's 'treasury' turns out to be an empty room where he prays, and an army captain miraculously arrives to deposit money with him. On the way home the man spends all he was given to ransom two Jewish women from a cruel noble's steward. That night an angel disguised as a merchant entrusts him with money for a man who does not exist, and the rebbe explains the money is his reward for his trust.
